The hypotheses n>=2k and q>=2 yield 0<R^2/v<1; precisely disjoint U,V contribute negative entries. Their count is D=q^{k^2}[n-k choose k]_q by graph-map parametrization. Zero row sum makes the infinity norm twice negative mass; symmetry gives equal column norm. Since diag=(v-1)/B>0 and complement diag=1-(v-1)/B>=0, the exact complement formula follows. For n=2k+s, D/B equals the stated ratio of finite (1-q^{-r}) products, and R/q^k→1/(q-1), (v-1)/(v-R)→1; establishes the limit, including q=2 and s=0. Independently checked 180 exact q-binomial parameter triples, including q=4 formal cardinalities; no finite test was substituted for universal proof. originality.rationale: The general orthogonal Grassmann projector kernel is already given in Marco–Parcet 2005: Theorem 3.6 gives q-Hahn polynomial spherical kernels in every harmonic degree, and Remark 5.5/eq. (23) identifies these kernels, with dimensions, as actual orthogonal projections. Specializing s=1 supplies the same first-degree linear-in-intersection kernel (up to the standard normalization). Its absolute row sum is then resolved by the elementary inequality [k]_q^2/[n]_q<1, the standard disjoint-subspace Gaussian-binomial count, and the standard matrix infinity-norm identity. The complementary norm changes only the diagonal; the fixed-excess Euler product is the Gaussian-binomial product limit. Thus all numerical conclusions are direct elementary corollaries of a substantially broader published same-object kernel theorem and routine counts, not an independently original mathematical result. Search alone is not the rejection basis.
residual_risks: The exact norm might independently appear in specialized q-Hahn Lebesgue-constant tables or old literature not indexed by searched sources; this is not necessary for the rejection because the broader published kernel implies it directly.
Dunkl, An Addition Theorem for Some q-Hahn Polynomials (1978), is cited by Marco–Parcet as an older full-kernel antecedent; its full text was not inspected.

The strength of the value judgment is specifically that this submission supplies an elementary after-the-fact evaluation of standard data; a deeper higher-degree or stability question might have independent value, but is not in this final claim.

value.rationale: A first primitive-idempotent endpoint norm is intrinsically a natural harmonic-analysis quantity, and its fixed-excess asymptotic is a neat explicit formula. However, for this specific degree-one case the full q-Grassmann projector kernel has been published for all degrees (Marco–Parcet 2005). The submitted sign analysis requires only the elementary bound R^2/v<1, the classical disjoint-subspace count and the row-sum-zero identity; the Euler product is the standard Gaussian-binomial product in the fixed-excess regime. It adds no new structural lemma, finite cutoff/classification, nontrivial analytic mechanism, or unavailable invariant beyond routine evaluation of existing complete kernel data. This is an instructive worked example, not a separately substantial exact invariant under the shared value bar. The verdict is not based on correctness, finite work, or reproducibility alone.
